object_description: overlapping L-shaped school complex with two wings of differing height
design_condition: Placed in the northwest corner, the two wings close the village edge, terminate the sports facility, and form a protected courtyard with the neighbouring retirement home opening toward the landscape.

positive.statement: The precise placement creates a protected courtyard with considerable quality for both user groups.

position.rationale: Central courtyard-forming void is legible in plan and bounded at ground level by both wings.

positive.statement: The building’s ends are cleverly narrowed to do justice to the local scale despite its large volume.

position.rationale: Tapered ends are visible at the wing extremities, reducing the apparent scale of the complex.

positive.statement: The careful internal organization and clear operational processes promise a high level of long-term usage value.

position.rationale: Internal planning is unshown, so the anchor is constrained to the main sampled building mass.

positive.statement: The multifunctional zones and autonomously usable areas provide valuable added flexibility.

position.rationale: Programmatic zones are not distinguishable; placement follows a plausible wing interior near the courtyard.

positive.statement: The large room depths are made workable through internal glazing between rooms and access zones.

position.rationale: Glazing and room depths are unshown, anchored approximately within the deeper courtyard-facing wing.

positive.statement: The construction combines regional traditional elements skilfully with contemporary timber construction.

position.rationale: Material identity is not separable, so the marker follows the visible south-facing exterior envelope.

positive.statement: The structural system, prefabricated ceilings, facades, and canopy meet the building-physics requirements.

position.rationale: The canopy edge is sampled, while structural and building-physics systems remain inferred from the exterior mass.

negative.statement: The project ultimately fails to meet the local architectural quality because of its height and consistent volumetric generosity.

position.rationale: Four-story height and generous overlapping volumes are evident across the plan and elevations.

negative.statement: The generous and complex construction generates added value but also costs.

position.rationale: Cost criticism has no useful spatial referent in the sampled geometry.

negative.statement: All details, especially the large cornices and interfaces, must be planned and executed very carefully to ensure long service life.

position.rationale: Cornice and interface detailing is approximated along the upper visible south facade edge.
